title: Indemnity cap matrix and sales-facing redline dashboard
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a single, sales-facing dashboard and supporting playbook that automates indemnity/liability cap decisions for inbound enterprise contract redlines, surfaces a defensible recommended position to Sales, and wires the output into the legal intake and routing flows. The deliverable combines: (1) a configurable indemnity cap matrix (by customer tier, product, and revenue), (2) an autotriage risk score that maps redline items to recommended concessions, and (3) a lightweight dashboard for Sales and Legal Ops showing recommendation, rationale, and required approval path.

Background:
Current handling of indemnity, liability, and consequential-loss redlines is slow and inconsistent. Sales often escalates identical asks that Legal treats differently depending on context. This increases cycle times and creates unpredictability for pricing/packaging experiments. We already have an intake form (PM-26789) and the contract redline routing playbooks, but there is no single source of truth for indemnity caps or an automated recommendation that Sales can rely on at negotiation time.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-approval for common indemnity and liability redlines by 40% for self-serve-eligible accounts.
- Standardize recommended caps across Sales and Legal for like-for-like customer profiles.
- Surface clear escalation steps and pre-approved concessions that map to pricing tiers and reserved capacity offers.
- Create telemetry to measure uplift and false-positives of recommendations.

Outcomes / Acceptance Criteria:
- Indemnity cap matrix defined and codified in a JSON/CSV lookup (configurable by Legal).
- Autotriage scoring implemented as a deterministic rule set (initially), with an interface for Legal to add/override rules via a Confluence-managed doc and backend CSV.
- Sales dashboard prototype that displays: request summary, recommended cap, confidence level (low/medium/high), approval path, and a one-click request escalation to Legal Ops.
- Documentation: playbook with examples (3 buyer scenarios), Slack routing patterns, and SLA expectations.
- Success metrics tracked: time-to-resolution, % auto-approved, number of manual escalations, and cost delta by concession.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Asha Patel (owner), Ethan Morales (assignee PM/PMM), Ravi Singh (Sales PM)
- Legal: Priya Nambiar (lead), Jordan Lee (Legal Ops)
- Engineering: ENG-4210 (Legal intake) - tech lead: Mara Kline
- Sales: Enterprise AEs pilot cohort

High-level approach:
1) Discovery (2 sprints): interview Legal/AE reps, audit last 18 months of redlines, identify 80% of common indemnity patterns.
2) Definition: build indemnity cap matrix (CSV), map to customer tiers and product SKUs.
3) Autotriage rules authoring: start with rule-based engine in Lambda; deterministic rules with confidence heuristics and explicit override flags.
4) Dashboard: lightweight React page in Console under Legal Tools; Sales role has read/submit rights.
5) Rollout: pilot with 5 AEs, iterate for 4 weeks, then expand to all Enterprise AEs.

Out of scope:
- Full ML-based classifier (future work).
- Automatic contract signature or bilateral document edits without Legal Ops approval.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly aggressive automation recommends concessions that increase liability exposure. Mitigation: start conservative; default "needs legal review" for caps above threshold; require Legal sign-off for high-revenue accounts.
- Risk: Sales ignores dashboard because it slows negotiations. Mitigation: embed one-click escalation and provide pre-approved language for counters.
- Risk: Configuration drift between Legal and Sales. Mitigation: single source of truth stored in Git + Confluence changelog and a monthly sync.

Next steps:
- Kickoff meeting with Legal and Sales ops (scheduled 2026-03-16).
- Engineering spike for integration with intake form (ENG-4210) due 2026-03-24.
- Draft indemnity cap matrix v0 (Legal) due 2026-03-20.

implementation_notes: Start with rule-based deterministic mapping. Use existing intake fields (customer_tier, expected_commit, product_family, international_presence) as inputs. Store canonical matrix in Git and surface update requests through Confluence-to-Git flow. Dashboard to call /legal/autotriage endpoint and show recommended action and confidence. Enforcement: create Slack channel and webhook for urgent escalations.
qa_criteria: Unit tests for rule mappings, e2e for intake->recommendation flow, manual test cases for three buyer scenarios documented in the playbook, load test for dashboard call at 100 rps (read-only).
monitoring_and_telemetry: Emit events: redline_autotriage.request, redline_autotriage.decision, redline_autotriage.escalation with tags (customer_tier, revenue_band, product_family). Dashboards: autotriage acceptance rate, mean time to resolution, manual escalation rate.
pilot_plan: Pilot cohort: 5 AEs, 4-week pilot. Metrics check-in at week 1, 2, and 4. Auto-approve threshold initially conservative: revenue < $250k and cap <= $250k. Expand thresholds after legal sign-off.
communication_plan: Launch notes to Sales and Legal Ops via Email and #legal-ops Slack thread. Training: 30-minute demo session and one-pager playbook. Follow-up office hours in first 2 weeks.
